insight: SSIM vs goldens lands at ~0.998 across runs (cursor position noise is negligible); run-to-run t_agent spread was 9278-9334 on runs 2-3 with run 1 warmer at 11554 — median of 3 absorbs the cold-start outlier.

idea: idea 1: warm verb (pre-boot daemon+recorder, start attaches)
insight: The frozen bench calls `start` directly and would never exercise a separate `warm` command, so the perceived-zero start can never show up in T_agent under this harness. Any warm-path win must instead come from making `start` itself cheaper (ideas 2/3) or from a harness change (needs human sign-off, like idea 16).

idea: idea 3: start-path poll tightening (ping 150→50ms, waitForFile 200→50ms, connectCdp 300→100ms, recorder post-goto 300ms sleep removed)
insight: 606ms (6.5%) came purely from poll granularity and a dead insurance sleep — no behavior change, SSIM unchanged (~0.998). Run 1 was 10750ms (cold after daemon-code change) and median-of-3 absorbed it again; the post-goto 300ms sleep in recorder.mjs was pure latency since the ready-file is only written after it, and G1/G2/G6 confirm listeners attach fine without it. Remaining start cost is dominated by Chromium boot itself, so idea 2 (persistent browser) is the next lever on this phase.
